speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand your wife is concerned about your recent bizarre and agitated behavior; let's start by asking, have you experienced any hallucinations or hearing voices lately?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old male. The patient has been demonstrating bizarre and agitated behavior for the past 6 weeks. He believes that he is being spied on by the NSA which is also controlling his mind. His wife adds that he has been increasingly withdrawn and intermittently depressed over the last 3 months. He was terminated from his job 4 weeks ago after he ceased attending work. Since his unemployment, he has been focused on creating a device to prevent people from controlling his mind.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a concerning belief; can you tell me if you have ever heard voices speaking directly to you, or if you see things others do not? Also, have you experienced any significant loss of interest in activities you used to enjoy, aside from your work?

speaker: Patient
text: creating a device to prevent people from controlling his mind. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Delusional Disorder, Persecutory Type.

The patient presents with a 6-week history of a fixed, false belief of persecution (being controlled/spied on by the NSA) without prominent hallucinations or disorganized behavior, alongside recent occupational impairment and depressive symptoms. These features are characteristic of Delusional Disorder, Persecutory Type, rather than Schizophrenia or a primary mood disorder.
